title: Liczby 5+ · dopełniacz
note: The numeral-government rule deferred from a1_numbers, now payable because both plural forms exist: 2/3/4 + Nominative plural (a2_plural_nom), 5 and up + Genitive plural (a2_gen_pl). Three frames only — money, shopping quantities, time amounts. Every genitive plural in this file comes from a2_gen_pl's verified list (domow, piw, kaw, zup, godzin, minut, filmow, sklepow); no new stem-changing forms were derived. NO PEOPLE-COUNTING anywhere — virile numerals (pieciu) are B1. Four small teaching additions, all reported as forks: (1) dwie, the feminine of two, because the unit cannot state its own rule without inviting the error *dwa kawy; (2) godziny and minuty, the plain plurals the time frame needs on the 2-4 side; (3) dolary/dolarow, one ordinary masculine money noun so that euro reads as the exception it is rather than as the rule; (4) lat and lata as whole words, the Ile masz lat? payoff. rok -> lata/lat is suppletive and is explicitly taught whole, never derived — a2_gen_pl fenced it and that fence holds. The teens caution (11-19 behave as 5-and-up) is stated once in the intro and drilled in exactly one quiz item. 5+ phrases never stand as the subject of a verb in this pack, because that would need the neuter-singular agreement rule (B1); they appear only as objects of mam / ma / chce.

intro.title: The number decides the noun
intro.body:
You now have two plural forms of every noun, and the number in front of it chooses between them.

2, 3, 4 take the plain plural — the subject form you learned first.
5 and up take the genitive plural — the short one.

That is the whole rule. It works on every noun you know, and it never changes.
intro.body_pl: 2, 3, 4 + mianownik liczby mnogiej. 5 i więcej + dopełniacz liczby mnogiej.

intro.title: Two has a second form: dwie
intro.body:
Only the number two does this, and only in front of a feminine noun — the -a words.

masculine and neuter: dwa domy · dwa piwa · dwa koty
feminine: dwie kawy · dwie zupy · dwie godziny

Trzy and cztery never change. Nothing from five upwards changes either. This is the one extra form you have to remember, and the noun after it still takes the plain plural, because two is in the 2–4 group.
intro.body_pl: Rodzaj męski i nijaki: dwa. Rodzaj żeński: dwie. Trzy i cztery bez zmian.

intro.title: Money: euro never changes
intro.body:
Euro is a free gift. It is the same word after every number — nothing is added and nothing comes off:

dwa euro · pięć euro · sto euro

Do not take it as the pattern. Most money words are ordinary nouns and the rule applies to them in full — dolar behaves exactly like dom and telefon:

trzy dolary · pięć dolarów
intro.body_pl: Euro nigdy się nie zmienia: dwa euro, pięć euro, sto euro. Dolar odmienia się normalnie: trzy dolary, pięć dolarów.

intro.title: Ordering: how many do you want?
intro.body:
This is where you will use the rule most. Chcę takes the object form, and in the plural the object form is the same as the plain plural — so after 2, 3, 4 nothing extra happens at all:

Chcę dwa piwa. · Chcę trzy kawy.

From five upwards the genitive plural takes over, and it takes the object slot with it:

Chcę pięć piw. · Chcę sześć kaw.
intro.body_pl: Chcę dwa piwa. Chcę trzy kawy. Chcę pięć piw. Chcę sześć kaw.

intro.title: Time — and the rule you already use
intro.title_pl: Czas — i zasada, którą już znasz
intro.body:
Time amounts behave like everything else: trzy godziny, cztery minuty, sześć godzin, pięć minut.

Now the payoff. You have been using this rule since your very first lessons, in the one place it matters most — your age.

Ile masz lat? · Mam dwadzieścia lat. · Mam czterdzieści cztery lata.

That is this rule and nothing else. Twenty is in the 5-and-up group, so the year word goes genitive plural: lat. Forty-four ends in four, so it takes the plain plural: lata. You learned both whole, and now you know why they are different.

Rok is the one word here you cannot build. Its plural is lata and its genitive plural is lat — irregular, learn the two whole.

One caution: the teens, 11 to 19, all count as five-and-up, however they end. Dwanaście lat, not dwanaście lata.
intro.body_pl: Ile masz lat? Mam dwadzieścia lat. Mam czterdzieści cztery lata. rok → lata (2–4) / lat (5+).

quiz.explain: Two, three and four keep the plain plural — the same form you use as a subject. Piw is the genitive plural and only appears from five upwards.
Five and everything above it hands the noun to the genitive plural. Piwa would have been right after dwa, trzy or cztery, and neuter nouns never take -ów.
Kawa is feminine, and two is the only number with a feminine form. The noun stays in the plain plural, because two sits in the 2–4 group.
Six is in the 5-and-up group, so the genitive plural — and a feminine noun takes no ending there at all. The word simply stops.
The genitive plural has been reached for one number too early. Three is still in the 2–4 group, so the plain plural stands.
Euro is the same word after every number. It is the one money word that costs you nothing — but it is the exception, not the pattern.
Dolar is an ordinary masculine noun, so it does exactly what dom and telefon do: -ów after five and up. Only euro escapes.
You already say this in Mam dwadzieścia lat. Ten is in the 5-and-up group, so the year word takes its genitive plural — and that form is lat, not anything built from rok.
Four is in the 2–4 group, so the plain plural. This is why you say Mam czterdzieści cztery lata and not lat — the number ends in four.
The teens, 11 to 19, all count as five-and-up however they end. Twelve ends in two but it does not behave like two.
Feminine noun, 5-and-up group, so the genitive plural with no ending on it. Godziny is what you would say after trzy or cztery.

type_items.explain: Feminine noun, so two is dwie. The noun itself does not react to that — it is the plain plural, exactly as it would be after trzy.
Nothing about money makes a noun special. Dolar ends in a hard consonant, so the genitive plural is -ów, the same ending as domów and telefonów.
Euro is one of a handful of words Polish borrowed and then left alone. There is no ending to choose, after any number.
Rok is irregular and you learn its plural whole: lata after 2, 3, 4, and lat from five upwards. There is no rule that builds either one out of rok.

use_items.explain: Chcieć normally takes the object form, but from five upwards the number outranks it and the noun goes genitive plural instead.
Four is in the 2–4 group, so the plain plural stands — and the plain plural is already the object form, so nothing else happens to the word.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: There are four shops here.
Type: Anna is twenty years old.
use_items.explain: The same sentence you already say about yourself, with a name in front of it. Twenty is in the 5-and-up group, so the year word is lat.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Dad is forty-four years old.
use_items.explain: The number ends in four, so it is in the 2–4 group and the year word is lata. Change it to forty-five and it would be lat again.
